name: Transatlantic Championship
epitaph: AWC's Transatlantic Championship was first won by Alexander Strider on 6 May 2005. The fed's own record carries 10 reigns on it, across 7 different champions. The longest is Pierce Lavelle's, 140 days from 30 August 2005. One of its reigns ended outside a match — vacated. Darcy Crisis held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: Frontier Championship
epitaph: AWC's Frontier Championship was first won by Tim Shipley on 9 August 2005. The fed's own record carries 12 reigns on it, across 10 different champions. The longest is Ellis Nash's, 91 days from 24 March 2006. One of its reigns ended outside a match — vacated. Jack Murphy held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: Relentless Championship
epitaph: AWC's Relentless Championship was first won by Crimson O'Malec on 7 June 2005. The fed's own record carries 7 reigns on it, across 7 different champions. The longest is Red Rock's, 178 days from 7 March 2006. One of its reigns ended outside a match — vacated. Jack Murphy held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: Alliance Championship
epitaph: AWC's Alliance Championship was first won by Emerald Isle on 1 July 2005. The fed's own record carries 6 reigns on it, across 5 different champions. The longest is Emerald Isle's, 151 days from 1 July 2005. One of its reigns ended outside a match — vacated. The Coalition held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: Livewire Championship
epitaph: AWC's Livewire Championship was first won by The Educator on 5 July 2005. The fed's own record carries 6 reigns on it, across 6 different champions. The longest is The Educator's, 49 days from 5 July 2005. One of its reigns ended outside a match — vacated. AWC disbanded it on 24 December 2005 and reinstated it in September 2006. Scott Taylor held it at the end of the surviving record.

events.note: The fed's own title history disbands the Livewire Championship after Winter Warfare and reinstates it in September 2006, with the first return champion decided at Untouchable.

name: Countdown Trophy
epitaph: AWC's Countdown Trophy was first won by Teresa Tomas on 23 June 2006. The fed's own record carries 4 reigns on it, across 4 different champions. The longest is Vince Jones's, 35 days from 4 July 2006. One of its reigns ended outside a match — retired with the belt. AWC discontinued it on 1 September 2006.

events.note: The fed's own title history ends the trophy at Coast To Coast with the note "end of summer; trophy discontinued".
